item.title: Binance says resuming withdrawals after major hack
item.description: Binance said Sunday that it had resumed withdrawals after a major hack that affected more than $6 billion in funds. Binance, which is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes, had suspended user withdrawals after the attack. “First batch network now opened in phase one of withdrawals is $BTC bitcoin network,” Binance said on X. The company said in an earlier update that it was preparing to resume the first phase of withdrawals between 0600 and 0900 GMT on Sunday. “We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand, so that each network and asset pair can be restored carefully, with stability and security checks completed before access is reopened,” it said. Binance said Saturday that it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses in the hack, which is thought to be the biggest-ever crypto heist. “User funds remain safe. Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users,” it said on X. The FBI accused North Korea of being behind the attack on Saturday, confirming earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a Pyongyang-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack. The hack is the latest in a string of high-profile cyber thefts linked to North Korea, which has built a formidable hacking operation, generating funds believed to help finance its weapons program. News of the cyberattack caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday. The post Binance says resuming withdrawals after major hack appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Trump says US still has ‘one or two targets’ in Iran
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Saturday that the United States has knocked out much of Iran’s military but still has to “take care of” one or two targets, as Tehran warned of reprisals if attacked. Trump maintained that negotiations with Iran to end the war, which was started by the United States and Israel in February, were “going fine but you know they’re not very reliable.” The Republican president said the United States is not in a hurry to take offensive action because it had already decimated Iran’s military and nuclear program. “We’ve knocked out their nuclear. We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Trump told reporters at his Florida residence. “You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex. The Iranian government denied any nuclear work is carried out there. Earlier Saturday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran and that the United States would be open to a diplomatic solution. Iran’s supreme leader on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against launching a new offensive, following threats they could resume strikes after crucial elections in both countries. Trump had previously warned an attack could come after the US midterms this week, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke of a “historic, one-time opportunity” to topple the Iranian government. The elections in both countries could determine the direction of the conflict, with Israel having voted in a general election on Tuesday but yet to form a new government. “Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response,” Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei told top military commanders, according to a statement. Khamenei also ordered commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy”. This was the first reported meeting between Khamenei and military top brass. The supreme leader has not been seen publicly since before he took the helm in March, after the killing of his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in US-Israeli strikes. – Oil price spike – Rubio warned that “we can achieve military objectives if we seek to”, adding that Trump had not made a decision on any fresh strikes. Since the recent outbreak of the war, Tehran has restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries around one-fifth of global oil consumption. Iran has previously warned it would also consider severing undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz. A ship traversing the strait struck a mine and caught fire, Iranian state television reported Saturday. item.title: Trump intervenes as Ghana demands justice over killing of 15-year-old boy in US
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has agreed to facilitate a visa for the Ghanaian mother of Javits Frimpong, a teenager killed while walking to school in New York. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Trump’s intervention on Saturday, as Ghana demanded justice for 15-year-old Frimpong, whose killing has shaken the Bronx. “The murder of a child is a pain no parent should have to endure, let alone from thousands of miles away,” Mamdani declared. The mayor said Trump agreed during their telephone conversation to grant a visa immediately to the teenager’s mother, Doris Gyamfi, who lives in Kumasi, Ghana. However, the White House had not independently confirmed the arrangement, and it remained unclear whether the visa had been issued by Saturday evening. Frimpong was shot in the abdomen around in the morning in Bronx’s neighbourhood. Police officers rushed him to St. Barnabas Hospital, where he was pronounced dead while investigators began searching for three suspected teenage assailants. The teenager had moved from Ghana in October 2025 to reunite with his father, Thomas Frimpong, hoping to pursue his education and build a promising future. “He was very clever, so he always says he wants to be a physician,” his grieving father told newsmen in New York. The elder Frimpong said his son had complained of persistent bullying at DreamYard Preparatory School, where two students were reportedly suspended, although police have not established any connection to the killing. Ghana’s Foreign Affairs Minister, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, subsequently contacted the bereaved father, conveying condolences from President John Dramani Mahama and promising government support. “We will pursue justice, and we will make sure that those who did this do not get away with it,” Ablakwa declared. Ghanaian diplomats in New York visited the family while the government demanded a thorough investigation and pledged legal and consular assistance to secure accountability. Following Mamdani’s announcement, Ablakwa welcomed Trump’s intervention and disclosed that Ghana would finance the mother’s travel, assist with visa arrangements and support funeral expenses. “The Government of Ghana welcomes your intervention and President Trump’s timely decision,” Ablakwa said, acknowledging the cooperation between the American and Ghanaian authorities. Bronx Congressman Ritchie Torres also expressed grief, saying: “Our entire borough is mourning a young man who should have had his whole future ahead of him.” The New York City Department of Education offered counselling and cooperation with investigators, stating: “Our hearts are with this young person’s family and school community during this unimaginably difficult time.” Meanwhile, vigils brought together Ghanaian residents, religious leaders and neighbours demanding justice on Saturday as police continued investigating the killing without announcing arrests or establishing a motive. item.title: WARRI DELINEATION: UIY challenges INEC over disputed wards
item.description: Ugbarajo Itsekiri Youths, UIY, has demanded that the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, provide the legal and geographical basis for the Warri Federal Constituency units and ward delineation data it uploaded. UIY said the report had potential implications for community identity, representation, political participation and public confidence in democratic institutions, particularly amid allegations of electoral boundary manipulation. The group’s National Public Relations Officer, Gbubemi Ejesi, said Itsekiri youths regarded the disputed developments as a serious threat to electoral justice, the political representation of indigenous communities and peaceful coexistence in Warri. According to him, the recently uploaded electoral structure, including the reported inclusion of locations and units whose geographical and administrative assignments are being challenged, had raised disturbing questions about INEC’s methodology, the authenticity of the geographical coordinates used and the extent to which the exercise complied with applicable judicial decisions. The statement reads: “UIY expresses its strongest condemnation of the alleged irregularities surrounding the recent ward delineation data uploaded by INEC for Warri Federal Constituency, Delta State. “We regard the disputed developments as a serious threat to electoral justice, the political representation of indigenous communities, and peaceful coexistence in Warri. The recently uploaded electoral structure, including the reported inclusion of locations and units whose geographical and administrative assignments are being challenged, has raised disturbing questions about INEC’s methodology, the authenticity of the geographical coordinates used, and the extent to which the exercise complies with applicable judicial decisions. “Of particular concern is the allegation that the disputed delineation is being used to establish an electoral and political presence for Ijaw interests in areas of Warri South, where UIY maintains that such a community-based political structure did not previously exist. Warri cannot be subjected to an electoral arrangement that indigenous communities believe disregards their history, established territorial interests, and legitimate political rights for non-indigenous ethnic groups. “The Ugbarajo Itsekiri Youths reject the disputed Warri Federal Constituency delineation report recently uploaded by INEC. We are particularly concerned about the reported creation of three disputed wards allegedly carved out of ancestral Okere and Pessu lands, which UIY maintains are historic Itsekiri territories. “We strongly challenge any attempt to alter the electoral structure of these areas without a transparent, lawful, and verifiable process consistent with applicable judicial decisions. “Our concern is not merely about the names assigned to wards or polling units. item.title: New tax laws outlaw revenue roadblocks, Adesokan says
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief There is no room for agents of state and local governments to mount roadblocks in the name of revenue collection under the new tax laws, the Executive Secretary of the Joint Revenue Board (JRB), Mr Olusegun Adesokan, has said. Adesokan stated this in Abuja last week while reviewing the implementation of the new tax laws, saying the harmonised legislation was designed to curb multiple taxation and illegal revenue collection across the country. He said the board was working with the police to tackle illegal revenue collectors who mount roadblocks, harass motorists and impose unauthorised charges on transporters along highways. According to him, illegal revenue collection has become a major contributor to the high cost of transporting goods across the country and would no longer be tolerated. The JRB executive secretary acknowledged that multiple taxation and harassment of traders and transporters remained widespread despite the ongoing reforms. “We know the problem exists, and we are working to fix it. We may not be able to clear everything completely today, but as time goes on, we are working on it,” he said. Adesokan explained that illegal roadside collections increase transportation costs, with the resulting burden passed on to consumers through higher food prices and the cost of other goods. He said the reforms were intended to address overlapping taxes and levies that increase the cost of doing business, adding that 21 of the 36 states had passed the relevant laws to facilitate their implementation. The states, according to him, are Kebbi, Kaduna, Zamfara, Ekiti, Enugu, Abia, Anambra, Gombe, Adamawa, Yobe, Borno, Niger, Plateau, Benue, Kogi, Kwara, Nasarawa, Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Delta and Ondo. He said the states yet to pass the legislation were at different stages of implementing the reforms, partly because of legislative processes and consultations with stakeholders. Adesokan said the board, which comprises tax authorities at the federal and state levels, was working to ensure uniform implementation of the new tax laws and eliminate arbitrariness in tax administration across the country. He stressed the need to support micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), describing them as the foundation of a fast-growing economy and an important part of the country’s business environment. He urged state tax authorities to respect the tax exemption provisions for small businesses and avoid actions that could undermine the reforms. Adesokan cited small traders and artisans among categories of taxpayers covered by applicable exemptions, saying tax authorities should focus on those with the capacity to pay rather than burdening low-income earners. He added that the board had issued guidelines to promote uniform personal income tax administration and harmonised tax practices across the states. item.title: Zamfara governor presents staff of office to 19 emirs
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State has presented staff of office and official vehicles to 19 newly coronated emirs in the state. The ceremony, held at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, the state capital, was attended by the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Sa’ad Abubakar; the Etsu Nupe; and the Emir of Gwandu, among other dignitaries. Following their oaths of office, Lawal presented staff of office to 11 first-class emirs and eight second-class emirs. Each of the 19 emirs also received three official vehicles: a GAC ULTRA SUV (2025/2026 model), a MIKANO ZNA HILUX vehicle and an EV ANTIQUE MODEL car (DDP). The vehicles, according to the state government, are intended to facilitate the emirs’ movements within their domains and enable closer engagement with their communities. Speaking at the ceremony, Lawal said the presentation reflected his administration’s recognition of the traditional institution as an enduring part of society and a key partner in promoting peace, stability and development. He said the ceremony also reaffirmed his government’s commitment to giving traditional rulers the recognition and institutional support required to discharge their responsibilities effectively. “The staff of office being presented today signifies the authority entrusted to you by the state. It also represents a responsibility to govern your respective domains with fairness, wisdom, integrity and compassion,” he said. The governor urged the emirs to discharge their duties without discrimination, uphold justice and ensure that their palaces remained accessible to all members of their communities. “Our people must find guidance, fairness and reassurance in their traditional rulers,” he said. Lawal also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to completing the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the remaining royal palaces, describing them as important centres of traditional authority and community engagement. On the vehicles presented to the emirs, he urged them to maintain and use them responsibly in the discharge of their official duties. The governor further called on the traditional rulers to build productive partnerships between their respective emirates and the state government. Earlier, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Sa’ad Abubakar, urged the newly coronated emirs to remain loyal to the constituted authority and uphold the dignity of the traditional institution in the discharge of their responsibilities. item.title: AI-Generated Pregnancy Claims: Nollywood’s Annabel Apara laments price of fame in deepfake era
item.description: By Prisca Sam-Duru It started with pictures. Then videos on social media. In both, Nollywood actress Annabel Apara appeared visibly pregnant, smiling, cradling a bump that never existed. She was even seen purportedly sharing announcements and clips documenting a pregnancy journey. Within hours, the images were everywhere – shared on WhatsApp groups, reposted on blogs, debated in comment sections. The only problem? It was all fake. That’s what an AI deepfake can do. “I’ve been seeing a lot of AI-generated pictures and videos of me being supposedly ‘pregnant,’ and that isn’t true,” Apara said, breaking her silence on the viral fabrication. For the fast-rising actress, who broke into Nollywood in 2024 and has been steadily building a name for herself, the experience was both bewildering and worrying. How quickly people believed it. How fast they shared it. She is not alone. Across the world, actors, musicians and public figures are waking up to find their faces, voices and bodies cloned by artificial intelligence – used to sell products, endorse politicians, or, as in Apara’s case, manufacture a pregnancy announcement. But for young female celebrities in Nollywood, the violation feels more personal. It is not just an image; it is their body, their privacy, their story being rewritten without consent. Apara’s response was measured but firm: disregard it, and verify. The actress, a content creator as well as an actor, urged fans to stop the cycle of “see it, believe it, share it” and instead check her verified handles before accepting any news about her as truth. “Verify claims about me through my official, verified social media accounts,” she said. The message is simple, but in an age of hyper-realistic AI, it is increasingly urgent. If the incident revealed the dark side of technology, it also revealed Apara’s focus. At a time when many would be drawn into an online war of words with bloggers, the actress has chosen to keep her eyes on the work. Currently studying English Arts at the University of Lagos, Apara is part of a new generation of Nollywood talents who refuse to be boxed in. She acts, she creates content, she writes, she produces. For her, storytelling does not end when the director shouts “cut.” Her credits already include “After School”, “One Night Guests”, “Walls Apart”, “Along Came Love”, “Danfo Dreams”, “Campus Chronicles”, “Campus Queen” and “Love Denied” – a growing list that has earned her attention since she came under the mentorship of actress and producer Ruth Kadiri. “I am committed to growing across multiple areas of the entertainment industry,” she says, describing a career ambition that lives both in front of and behind the camera. And to the fans who reached out, who asked rather than assumed, she is grateful. For Annabel Apara, the fake baby bump will fade from timelines in a few days. Another AI scandal will take its place. item.title: SAHCO to handle Air Algérie flights in Lagos, Abuja
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Skyway Aviation Handling Company Plc, SAHCO, has secured a ground handling contract with Air Algérie in Lagos and Abuja. Under the agreement, SAHCO will provide full ground handling services to Air Algérie at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos and the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja, leveraging its highly trained workforce, modern ground support equipment and operational expertise to deliver safe, seamless and efficient services in line with international best practices. Commenting on the development, the Chairman of SAHCO Plc, Taiwo Afolabi, expressed delight at the partnership, describing the contract as a testament to the company’s growing reputation for operational excellence and dependable service delivery. He said: “We are delighted that Air Algérie has chosen SAHCO as its ground handling partner in Lagos and Abuja. This confidence reflects our unwavering commitment to safety, operational efficiency and service excellence. We remain focused on delivering seamless ground handling solutions that meet the expectations of our airline partners and contribute to a superior passenger experience.” The post SAHCO to handle Air Algérie flights in Lagos, Abuja appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Imo West ruling could cost Tinubu South-East votes, APC group warns
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — A pro-Tinubu group, Renewed Hope Foot Soldiers for Tinubu (RHFST), has warned that the Federal High Court’s ruling recognising Rochas Okorocha as the duly elected All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo West Senatorial District could heighten political tensions in the South-East and undermine President Bola Tinubu’s support ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group’s National President, Hon. Gbenga Owojori, who raised the concern in a statement issued on Saturday in Abuja, said the dispute had implications beyond the senatorial constituency, particularly for the political calculations surrounding the Senate presidency. “The dispute over the Imo West ticket has consequences beyond the constituency. It has altered the political calculations surrounding the Senate presidency and raised concern that a leading South-East contender could be shut out of the contest before the next Senate is constituted,” the group said. It argued that Governor Hope Uzodimma, a former senator, should be allowed to pursue his political ambitions in accordance with established rules. According to the group, Uzodimma’s supporters consider him a credible contender for the Senate presidency, with backing from political leaders across party lines. The group also drew attention to allegations by critics that Senate President Godswill Akpabio had an interest in preventing Uzodimma from emerging as a potential rival, while former Rivers State Governor and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, was allegedly involved in efforts to pursue a legal challenge against the Imo governor. It said the allegations had been linked by critics to Akpabio’s previous support for Wike during his political disagreement with Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara. The group further expressed concern over allegations that Wike may have influenced the court proceedings, citing claims by Uzodimma’s supporters that the FCT minister had repeatedly threatened to deal with the Imo governor. However, RHFST cautioned against treating the allegations as established facts, insisting that the judgment should be assessed on its legal merits. “These are serious claims and should not be treated as established facts. The judgment must be assessed on its legal merits, and the statements attributed to Wike require clarification. Given the political consequences of the ruling, the public deserves confidence that no political pressure has influenced the judicial process,” it said. The group maintained that Uzodimma should be assessed on his political record, experience and support base, rather than being denied an opportunity to pursue his ambitions. It urged the APC to ensure transparency in its nomination processes and avoid actions that could be perceived as excluding candidates to protect the political interests of others. item.title: 2027: Presidency should remain in South until 2031 — BTO For PBAT
item.description: Group says move will strengthen national unity, political stability, democratic inclusiveness By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Director-General of BTO For PBAT ’27 Support Group, Ogbeni Adojutelegan Adesuyi Gideon, has said the presidency should remain in Southern Nigeria until 2031 to promote equity, fairness and political balance. Adojutelegan said allowing the South to complete an eight-year presidential tenure would strengthen national unity, sustain democratic stability and give all geopolitical zones a sense of belonging. In a statement issued in Akure, he acknowledged that power rotation was not expressly provided for in the Constitution but argued that it remained an important political arrangement for sustaining national cohesion and strengthening democratic institutions. He said the issue should be approached with political maturity and a commitment to the stability of the federation. The group, which operates under the leadership of the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said equitable political arrangements were essential to sustaining mutual trust and deepening democracy. Adojutelegan described the return of power to the South in 2023 as significant, arguing that allowing the region to complete eight years in 2031 would serve the interest of political balance. “The position of BTO For PBAT ’27 is clear and unequivocal: the presidency of the Federal Republic of Nigeria should remain in the South until 2031. “This position is not founded on sectional sentiment or regional antagonism. It is anchored on the fundamental principles of equity, fairness, justice and the need to sustain mutual understanding among the various geopolitical zones that constitute our great nation. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu assumed office on May 29, 2023. We believe that allowing the South to complete an eight-year presidential tenure, subject to the sovereign decision of Nigerians at the ballot box in 2027, would reinforce the spirit of fairness and political accommodation,” he said. He maintained that Nigeria’s democratic stability depended not only on constitutional provisions and elections but also on leaders’ willingness to uphold inclusion, balance and mutual respect. While acknowledging the constitutional right of every qualified Nigerian to contest elections, he urged political stakeholders to consider arrangements that would strengthen public confidence in the fairness of the political system. “The presidency is a national institution that belongs to all Nigerians. Its leadership must continue to reflect the aspirations, collective interests and democratic expectations of the federation. “We must recognise that political stability is strengthened when the various sections of the country believe that their interests are respected and their legitimate aspirations are fairly accommodated. “Our advocacy for the continuation of a southern presidency until 2031 is therefore a call for political fairness, national understanding and democratic consolidation,

item.title: Immigration requirements hit African travellers hardest — IATA
item.description: By Dickson Omobola International Air Transport Association, IATA, has released the results of its 2026 Global Passenger Survey, GPS, revealing, among other findings, that immigration requirements have discouraged passengers from visiting certain destinations. IATA, which highlighted two other major trends in passenger behaviour and expectations, said travellers were embracing biometric identification to reduce repeated document checks and expressing strong interest in using digital passports for check-in and more personalised services during booking. The survey also found that artificial intelligence, AI, was changing how passengers planned their trips. From finding flights and comparing fares to discovering new destinations, passengers are increasingly incorporating AI into their travel planning. Speaking on the survey, IATA’s Senior Vice President, Operations, Safety and Security, Nick Careen, said: “Passengers are embracing technology to make travel easier. AI is becoming a mainstream travel planning tool, while biometrics and digital identity are creating a faster and more seamless airport experience. Yet many travellers continue to face barriers from complex immigration and visa processes. Governments can help by simplifying entry requirements, eliminating duplicate checks, and accelerating the issuance and acceptance of secure digital travel credentials.” According to the survey, nearly six in 10 passengers reported experiencing biometric identification at least once in the past 12 months, while satisfaction with the technology reached its highest level yet. Meanwhile, the survey showed that entry requirements were becoming a growing barrier to travel, even as passengers embraced technology. Immigration requirements had discouraged 43 per cent of passengers from visiting a destination, up from 33 per cent in 2025. Among passengers discouraged from travelling to a particular destination by geopolitical conflict, 72 per cent said safety was the main reason, while 13 per cent cited uncertainty over whether travel was possible. Of those deterred by immigration requirements, 53 per cent said the process was too complex. Privacy concerns and cost were less common reasons, accounting for 17 per cent each. IATA said African travellers were among the most satisfied with their travel experiences but were also the most likely to have been discouraged from visiting a destination by immigration requirements. item.title: A compelling case for second tenure of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
item.description: By Patrick Obahiagbon Students of American political history would be consensus ad idem with me that it was the “New Deal” of President Franklin Delano Roosevelt (FDR) of the United States of America (USA)1933 to 1945, that recalibrated the American political economy, redefined the relationship between the government and the masses of the people, and indeed , actualized the programmes of the welfare state as theorized by the nobel winning John Maynard Keynes. Government spending, job creation, policies for old-age pensions, unemployment insurance, insurance for widows and orphans as provided in the USA Social security Act of 1935 were the defining elements of the New Deal of President Franklin Delano Roosevelt. Indeed, FRD reportedly thought outside the box, and implemented these far- reaching economic reforms, which took the USA out of the world economic depression of the 1930s through to the end of the Second World War. Then the boom of the successive years followed. Today, the economy of the USA leads the rest of the World’ s economies with 32.6 trillion dollars Gross Domestic Product ( GDP). Just like FDR, the irreplaceable and irrepressible President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is taking Nigeria on the path of a New Deal. PBAT’s Renewed Hope Agenda is redefining Nigeria’s political economy, and particularly putting the economy on the trajectory of recovery. PBAT is firming up the Nigerian economy for production, and eventual industrialization. In this great leap, there must be pains. Excruciating pains, only comparable to a woman in the labour ward. Such is the work which PBAT is working on as it relates to the Nigerian economy today. He weaned himself of sentiments anchoraging on namby pambyism. item.title: Kidnapping horror in Edo:Woman, fellow kidnappers caught by CCTV to die
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu WHEN Governor Monday Okpebholo was sworn-in on November 12, 2024, he was said to have confided in a close aide that there were two things he detested and would not allow them fester in Edo State: Thugerry and cultism. Closely related to this was kidnapping and other violent crimes. To show that he was prepared to check these challenges, Okpebholo approached the state House of Assembly to strengthen the anti-cultism and anti-kidnapping laws which now provide that any building linked to kidnapping and cultism would be demolished while convicted kidnappers would face the death penalty. To make justice seamless and devoid of bureaucratic encumbrances, the governor approached the Chief Judge of the state to dedicate a court to the two issues of kidnapping and cultism. The test of the resolve of the governor against kidnappers and cultism happened on the morning of Sunday, June 14, 2026 when, in broad daylight at the popular Vegetable Market off Airport Road, dare-devil kidnappers, operating in a pepper red Lexus Jeep, alighted from their vehicle, shot the tyres of a parked Toyota Highlander to kidnap the occupant. The owner of the vehicle escaped but his wife was not lucky as the kidnappers went away with her. The video of the incident went viral on social media courtesy of a CCTV in a building opposite the area where the incident happened. With marching orders from Okpebholo and the Inspector General of Police, four suspects, including a female, were arrested a few days after in connection with the incident and they became the first test of the courts dedicated to kidnapping and cultism. Barely four months after the investigation and prosecution started, the four suspects, namely, Marvelous Isaac, Wisdom Michael, Rufus Emete Michael and Gift Rachael, the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Defendants, were found guilty of the Vegetable Market kidnap and three others in different parts of the state and capital and also being members of a secret cult, and sentenced to death by hanging or by lethal injection. The charge sheet was marked CD/S/06C/2026 between the state and four Defendants. The judgment was delivered on September 29, 2026 by Justice A. T. Momodu. It took Momodu over three hours, 30 minutes to deliver his judgment during which he attributed the success recorded by the prosecution to the CCTV in the opposite building and advised that there should be a deliberate effort to install them in business areas, public and even homes. He said the prosecution called seven witnesses while seven exhibits tendered in the trial of kidnapping, armed robbery, illegal possession of firearms, conspiracy, and membership of a secret cult among others. “I wish to place on record my profound appreciation to the private citizen whose CCTV captured the scene of the Vegetable Market kidnapping incident”, the trial judge said. “That singular act of installing CCTV in his premises provided evidence which assisted the police in the detection and proof of the crime

item.title: Anti-party claims:Wike, Soludo, Adeleke fight back
item.description: •CSOs knock PDP, APGA, Accord leaders By Luminous Jannamike, Dickson Omobola, Henry Obeta & Esther Onyegbula The decision by some opposition governors to align with President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign has raised questions about party loyalty, political survival and the ability of opposition parties to present a united front ahead of the 2027 general election. At the centre of the unfolding political drama are the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, who remains a member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP); Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA); and Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party. Findings by Sunday Vanguard showed that their political choices have placed their respective parties in a delicate position as they grapple with the implications of their members’ involvement in a campaign to return the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to power. Crisis Wike, a prominent PDP figure and former Rivers State governor, has maintained his support for Tinubu despite the protracted crisis within the PDP and his strained relationship with members of the party opposed to his position. Soludo, on his part, has had to navigate the implications of his political relationship with the President while remaining in APGA, a party with its own electoral ambitions and identity. Adeleke’s emergence under the Accord Party banner has also drawn attention to the political calculations surrounding his relationship with the Tinubu-led administration and the implications for his party. Although the circumstances surrounding the three politicians differ, their positions have triggered debate over whether opposition politicians can support the electoral ambitions of a rival party without undermining the platforms on which they built their political careers. Against the backdrop of the approaching 2027 elections, the development presents a test of the PDP, APGA and Accord Party’s capacity to manage internal disagreements, defend their political identities and determine the limits of acceptable conduct by their prominent members. It has also raised questions about the strength of party discipline in Nigeria, where political allegiances are frequently shaped by personal interests, strategic calculations and the search for relevance in the corridors of power. Also, many are unsure whether what the politicians have done amounts to anti-party activities. Constitution Accordingly, the constitutions of the affected parties, in various sections, spell out actions that could constitute anti-party activities. Specifically, Section 10(6) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Constitution provides that no member shall align with other parties or groups to undermine the party or any of its elected governments. item.title: Ebola scare in Adamawa: NCDC confirms negative tests
item.description: …Two suspected cases test negative after two rounds of laboratory tests By Chioma Obinna The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) last night said two suspected Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases in Adamawa State tested negative after two rounds of laboratory tests, assuring Nigerians that the confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) remains the only confirmed infection reported in the country. The agency said the two individuals, who presented with symptoms suggestive of Ebola in Yola, were isolated as public health authorities commenced investigations and appropriate response measures. In a press statement yesterday, the Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, said the report was received by the Adamawa State Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) in the early hours of October 30, 2026. He said samples collected from the individuals were subjected to laboratory testing to establish the cause of their illness, adding that both tested negative for Ebola after two rounds of testing. “Fortunately, the samples turned out negative for EBV after two rounds of testing,” Idris said. He clarified that there was currently no laboratory-confirmed Ebola case in Adamawa, stressing that the index case previously confirmed in the FCT remained the only confirmed case in Nigeria. “At this juncture, I wish to commend the efforts of the Adamawa State’s Commissioner for Health and his team for their proactive approach. NCDC will continue to provide appropriate technical support to the Adamawa State Government to strengthen their response operations,” he said. The latest development comes amid heightened public health vigilance following the confirmation of a Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja involving a traveller who arrived in Nigeria from Uganda. The emergence of the suspected cases in Adamawa had raised concerns about a possible spread of the disease, prompting the state and federal health authorities to activate investigation and precautionary measures. However, the negative laboratory results have ruled out Ebola infection in the two individuals, based on the tests reported by the NCDC. Idris urged Nigerians to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information or speculation about the situation. “We urge members of the public to remain calm and avoid sharing unverified information or speculation about the situation. The public is encouraged to obtain information from official government and public health communication channels,” he said. The NCDC director-general, however, emphasised the need for continued vigilance, noting that Ebola was a serious infectious disease requiring prompt identification, appropriate clinical management and effective infection prevention and control measures. item.title: I am no more your leader, Wike is: Fubara faces uncertain future after surrendering
item.description: By Daniel Abia, P/Harcourt With dexterity and some sense of candor, he strode purposefully along the red carpet isle to the podium. His assigned role for the day was unambiguously defined: To unveil the Rainbow Coalition candidates for the 2027 general elections in Rivers State. But unknown to many, Governor Siminalayi Fubara had a special announcement to make. First, he took a brisk eye scan through the sea of heads at the Yakubu Gowon Stadium, then announced: “I am no more your leader. Stop calling me ‘my leader, my leader’” The day was Tuesday, October 27, 2026, when a political group formed by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Mr Nyesom Wike, organized a rally which drew participants from the 23 local government areas of the state. They converged on the Yakubu Gowon Stadium Port Harcourt to display which candidate from the six-member political parties that constitute the Rainbow Coalition for the coming elections. Fubara was tactically chosen to perform the unveiling and handover the flag of the All Progressives Congress, APC, to Hon Ogundu Kingsley Chinda, the anointed governorship candidate of Wike. Fubara did not only surrender his potential second term as a sitting governor to Chinda but also relinquished his role as the political leader of Rivers to Wike. The governor veered off the track of duty and handed down a stern warning, or so it seemed, to his organic supporters who stood by him in thick and thin during the dark moment of the political crisis in Rivers, telling them unreservedly that he was no more their leader. “Let me say something here so that it will always help us while we move forward”, he started. “I’m aware there are some issues where some persons who followed me when we had the crisis when you’re in your meeting you say ‘my leader, my leader’. “We are now in one house. And because we have one house, there is no issue about who is the leader. “I might be your oga (governor) but we have a common leader now. So, please, going forward, this issue of ‘my leader, my leader, my leader’, I want it resolved here and now.” There was a cumulus of silence at first, then a deafening applause. Governors as leaders Way back in January 2025, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, through his Vice, Kasim Shettima, had declared that all APC governors were political leaders of the party in their states. The implication is that as the highest political position in the state, a governor is seen as a leader politically. Tinubu made this known during the defection of Governor Agbu Kefas of Taraba State from PDP to APC. That pronouncement also covered Fubara the moment he defected from the same PDP to APC on December 9, 2025 and picked the 001 registration number of the ruling party. item.title: Kane Misses Penalty After Ballon d’Or Feat As Bayern Held By Dortmund
item.description: Fabio Silva’s 89th-minute goal earned Borussia Dortmund a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich after Harry Kane missed a penalty in a see-saw Bundesliga clash on Saturday. Bayern were 1-0 up when Kane, playing his first match since winning the Ballon d’Or on Monday, rattled his second-half spot kick against the crossbar. Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy levelled shortly after, but Kane helped Bayern retake the lead when he set up a Dayot Upamecano goal. In the final minute, substitutes Konstantinos Karetsas and Silva combined to grab Dortmund a share of the spoils. “Coming back twice here in Munich is no easy feat. We earned a well-deserved point here today,” Dortmund coach Niko Kovac told Sky Germany, adding his side “never stopped believing in ourselves.” Dortmund’s Guinean forward #09 Serhou Guirassy (C) scores the 1-1 goal during the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) The result leaves the two sides level atop the Bundesliga table, with defending champions Bayern ahead on goal difference. It is just the fourth time in the past 18 ‘Klassiker’ matches that Bayern have not emerged victorious. In addition to the late draw, Bayern, who are without Vincent Kompany as he recovers from a virus, will be concerned by further injuries to their undermanned forward line ahead of Tuesday’s trip to Atletico Madrid. Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all subbed out on Saturday, with Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz already out with injury. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the draw appeared “costly”, with Saibari and Gnabry’s injuries “somewhat serious”. Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich, who returned after missing three matches after the sudden death of his father, said: “It’s been a really, really hard week, but you can forget during the game. “Other than the result today, you have to say we’re going through difficult moments right now, now with the injuries we picked up.” Kane was honoured pre-match with his Ballon d’Or shown to the Bayern faithful for the first time. Bayern Munich’s English forward Harry Kane shows his Ballon d’Or trophy to the fans prior to the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) Dortmund thought they had taken the lead with 35 minutes gone as Jobe Bellingham scored from close range, but VAR overturned the goal for offside. Bayern made Dortmund pay immediately when Konrad Laimer pounced on a poor Felix Nmecha pass and charged upfield to score. Bayern were better after the break and a Nmecha handball brought Kane to the spot, but the England captain rifled his shot against the crossbar. item.title: Clashes Erupt In France As Thousands Protest Cost Of Living, Inequality
item.description: A police officer in Paris was injured after being struck by a Molotov cocktail as clashes erupted in the capital and other cities during protests across France against soaring living costs and inequality. Hundreds of thousands of people, some dressed for Halloween, demonstrated across France in a third consecutive weekend of largely peaceful demonstrations. But the Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez pointed to an “extraordinary” level of violence from some, blaming far-left extremist groups for attacks on security forces. He described the throwing of a Molotov cocktail at a riot police officer in Paris as an “attempted murder,” adding that the officer had escaped with minor injuries. “We are fully prepared for those looking for confrontation tonight,” he added. After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police, AFP journalists saw. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges. ‘Engulfed In Flames’ Far-right leader Marine Le Pen said those responsible for the Molotov attack must be “punished with the utmost severity.” “The images of a police officer engulfed in flames after being targeted with incendiary devices are unbearable,” Le Pen said on X. A French riot gendarme mobile has flames rising up his uniform after being hit by a Molotov cocktail during a charge against demonstrators at the end of a demonstration part of a nationwide day of protests over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students organisations, in Paris on October 31, 2026. Photo by SAMEER AL-DOUMY / AFP A night-time curfew was to be imposed in the central Paris Republique and Chatelet-Les Halles neighbourhoods from 11:00 pm to 6:00 am on Saturday and Sunday. Police arrested more than 420 people across the country. The interior ministry said that “radical elements” in cities including Bordeaux, Toulouse and Marseille had attempted to enter city centres “with the aim of carrying out vandalism and looting”. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people. ‘Attack On Freedom’ Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, marched through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. item.title: German Police, Protesters Clash After ‘Gen Z’ Protest, Several Police Officers Injured
item.description: German police and protesters clashed across the country Saturday following massive youth-led protests, with authorities using water cannon and pepper spray as masked demonstrators hurled fireworks, stones and bottles. Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined protests nationwide that were organised by the group “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!). The demonstrations, inspired by similar movements in France and Italy calling for political elites to heed the concerns of the younger generation, were largely peaceful during the day. But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of protesters refused to disperse. Police were pelted with projectiles in the western city of Frankfurt, and responded by using water cannon and pepper spray as they sought to clear protesters. “Incidents of stones and fireworks being thrown at the emergency services continue to occur,” police said on X. “We are taking action against these troublemakers.” Police also used water cannon in the cities of Hamburg and Cologne after they said demonstrators targeted emergency service workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. ‘Boiling Point’ In Berlin, a protest that was not organised by the “GenZ regelt!” movement took place in the evening, with police reporting they were pelted with eggs and bottles. Police in the eastern city of Leipzig also used pepper spray after protests turned violent while a police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group. Police were reported to have made several arrests. Police detain a protester after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP The youth-led protests earlier in the day took place in a mostly peaceful and festive atmosphere, with some dressed in outfits ranging from dinosaurs to Batman as the demonstrations coincided with Halloween.They waved signs that read “Time for resistance”, and “Merz must go”, in reference to conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz. “I think it’s really important to show solidarity with all the other protests currently happening across Europe, including in France,” Milla, a 20-year-old student who only gave her first name, told AFP in Berlin. “I’ve been waiting for a long time for something to finally really happen, and for people to tackle this with a bit more force. I believe that today here is the first step.” Marius, a 23-year-old care worker, added that “politicians need to know about this… the situation is slowly reaching boiling point.” “I think we can all feel that this just isn’t working anymore,” he added. The movement’s complaints range from the high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians making decisions with apparently little regard for the younger generation. item.title: Katsina Debunks Campaign Violence Claims, Orders Probe Into Yankara Incident
item.description: The Katsina State Government has dismissed reports linking the incident that occurred in Yankara, Faskari Local Government Area, to Governor Dikko Radda’s Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign, describing such claims as false and misleading. In a statement, the government said preliminary findings showed that the disturbance stemmed from a disagreement between participants in a Maulud procession and security personnel over designated procession routes, resulting in confusion along a public street in Yankara. It stressed that the incident was entirely unrelated to thegovernor’s campaign activities or the Tinubu-Dikko campaign rally held in Faskari. According to the government, Governor Radda passed through Yankara without incident on his way to Faskari, where he paid a courtesy visit to the District Head’s Palace and was received by the district head and other traditional rulers. The governor, it said, later proceeded to the Faskari Local Government secretariat, where he inspected ongoing renovation works at the secretariat and council chambers before attending the campaign rally and interacting with residents and supporters. Governor Dikko Radda addresses a crowd of supporters at the Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign in Faskari Local Government Area of Katsina State on October 31, 2026. The state government urged relevant security agencies to carry out a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that those responsible are identified where necessary. In the statement signed by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Ibrahim Mohammed, the government appealed to residents to remain calm, uphold peace, and avoid spreading unverified information capable of causing unnecessary tension. Violence was reported in Yankara town on Saturday after suspected hoodlums attacked supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC), leaving several people injured and a campaign vehicle set ablaze. Eyewitnesses said the attackers allegedly ambushed APC supporters heading to Governor Radda’s campaign rally in Faskari, disrupting movement along the major road and causing panic among residents. Angry youths were also alleged to have blocked the route the campaign convoy was expected to use. item.title: Man City Stunned In 0-1 Home Loss To Brighton
item.description: Manchester City suffered a second straight Premier League defeat at the hands of Brighton with a 1-0 win as the Seagulls went close within two points of the leaders on Saturday. Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first-ever away win against City on their 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title. The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials. Fabian Hurzeler’s men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday. Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time. City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld, they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top-flight. Defeat for Maresca’s men means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday. The Red Devils were left to regret not taking advantage of a series of first-half chances to take the lead before they imploded in the second period. item.title: Africa’s First Ever Youth Olympics Open In Senegal
item.description: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympics ever to be held on African soil, opened Saturday in the Senegalese capital, marking an historic moment for the continent. Signs proclaiming “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates” are omnipresent across Dakar, which is hosting nearly 2,700 young competitors aged 14 to 17 from around the world. The event will see the return of Russian athletes to the Olympics and also includes a refugee team. Overall, the young athletes will compete across 25 sports and 153 medal events. “Today it’s not just a nation that is welcoming the Youth Olympic Games; it’s an entire continent that is opening its arms”, Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye told a sport and development summit Saturday ahead of the Games’ opening ceremony. Senegal’s Influencer and TikToker Khaby Lame carries the Youth Olympic Flame on the eve of the opening ceremony of the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar on October 30, 2026. Photo by PATRICK MEINHARDT / AFP The Games will not only celebrate champions but also “our collective capacity to transform sport into an economic and social engine”, he said, emphasising that 130 years of Olympic history had passed before the Olympic flame ever landed on African soil. Events ranging from athletics to beach wrestling, rugby sevens to breaking, will be held across eight venues in three locations. Dakar, the nearby suburb of Diamniadio and the beach town of Saly, located some 80 kilometres (50 miles) from the capital, will all host events. The Games are “showing the world our capacity (as Africa), a capacity that sometimes is underestimated”, International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry, a former Zimbabwean swimmer, said Saturday during the summit. According to Coventry, the opening ceremony will be televised live in more than 30 countries, with every African nation having committed to showing the Games live, she said. Sports Culture An opening ceremony Saturday evening in Diamniadio will kick off the Games. A total of 136 Senegalese athletes will participate in the Youth Olympics, with some 6,000 volunteers from Senegal helping put on the event. The West African nation is renowned for its sports culture, including its football team, traditional wrestling and surf scene. Football enthusiasts and young people often organise impromptu matches in the evenings or on weekends on the beach or in village squares. And as the day cools, hundreds of people flock to Dakar’s iconic coastal road, the Corniche, to run, do strength training or take part in group exercise. While a sense of excitement is beginning to stir in the capital, the fourth summer edition of the Youth Olympics has struggled to stoke wild enthusiasm across Senegal. Mexican athletes arrive with their suitcases at the Youth Olympic Village in Diamniadio, on October 29, 2026.
